PASS. The diff cleanly implements PMAT-065 (#65) and satisfies all acceptance criteria in `docs/roadmaps/roadmap.yaml`. `.github/workflows/gate.yml` defines `book-build` (pinned to mdBook v0.4.40 matching `pages.yml`, failing if `book/index.html` is missing or `pages <= 1`) and `gate` (`if: always()`, `needs: [book-build]`, failing if `needs` is empty or any needed job did not end in `success`). All receipt claims, planted-control run records (`docs/audits/PMAT-065-planted-runs.tsv`), and quorum artifacts (`quorum-PMAT-065-A-control.json`, `quorum-PMAT-065-B.json`, `quorum-PMAT-065-signoff-r1.json`) are committed and verified against git history.

Scope question answer: Yes, gating on `book-build` alone is right. `book-build` is the only check with a green history on `main`, whereas link check (#58), `mdbook test`, `test.yml` (#53, #56), and `pmat-dogfood.yml` have never had a green run on `main`. Adding broken checks to the required `gate` fan-in now would keep all PRs blocked from merging; requiring three green nights on `main` and an owner's explicit yes before adding a check to `gate.needs` is the right policy.
